newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Sen. Nickles says airline tax change likely.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Sen. Nickles says airline tax change likely.

text.p: Assistant Senate Majority Leader Don Nickles said he expected a proposed 10 percent tax on domestic legs of international flights would not be included in a final tax bill.
"I hope that we will be able to eliminate that," Nickles said. The House tax bill did not include the provision.
The Oklahoma Republican will be part of a group of lawmakers who will try to iron out differences in House and Senate tax legislation starting Friday.

The lost revenues could be "offset by an increase in the departure, arrival ticket (tax), which would apply to internationals as well as domestics so you don't put domestic (airlines) at a disadvantage to internationals," Nickles said.
The House bill has a provision that would impose a $15.50 per passenger fee for international departures and arrivals. Currently there is a $6 international departure fee.
